pull.title: Release: 32.0 translations update
pull.body:
This PR follows our [Release Process](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/fc4f35fdce4d65696be6bf34003dbcac1f2f64bf/doc/release-process.md) and concludes the translation-related work for this release cycle.

It is one of the steps required _before_ branch-off, as scheduled in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/33607.

Previous similar PR: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34718.

**A note for reviewers:**
The actual translations on Transifex are a moving target. As a result, your diff after running [`bitcoin-maintainer-tools/update-translations.py`](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/bitcoin-maintainer-tools/blob/main/update-translations.py) may differ.

events.body: If I run the update through claude it flags a bunch of regressions. How much should we care about them?

> If I run the update through claude it flags a bunch of regressions. How much should we care about them?

Depends on the regressions.

Is it possible these are due to #34808?

> > If I run the update through claude it flags a bunch of regressions.

I only asked Claude to check for malicious translations.

> > How much should we care about them?
> 
> Depends on the regressions.
> 
> Is it possible these are due to #34808?

#34808 was tested for interaction with Transifex's [Translation Memory Fill-up](https://help.transifex.com/en/articles/6224817-setting-up-translation-memory-fill-up) in the "experimental-do-not-translate" resource. I also observed its behaviour while uploading the "32.x" resource in #34525. Everything went flawlessly.

Those regressions were more likely introduced by translators. This can be verified once the affected languages and strings are provided.

Since we [delegated](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/590#issuecomment-2495112) translation to the Transifex community, there isn't much we can do on our side. However, I could reach out to the coordinators of some languages.
